description: Build a reproducible database of railway stations, route records, and map layers from the local China railway CSV and HOTOSM GeoJSON datasets.
steps: Run ./init.sh from the ChinaHSR_Simulation folder
Verify station-data.json contains thousands of stations with WGS84 coordinates
Verify route-data.json contains simulated HSR routes seeded by real train origin-destination records
Verify hsr-stations.geojson and hsr-rails.geojson are present for the Mapbox layers

description: Book real seats by station interval so a seat becomes available to another passenger after the previous passenger gets off.
steps: Quote a train trip between two stations
Confirm a booking and receive a ticket ID, seat ID, car, row, seat letter, and price
Verify overlapping bookings cannot use the same seat interval
Verify a later passenger can reuse the same seat after the first passenger alights

description: Calculate realistic ticket prices from distance, seat class, segment occupancy, booking horizon, peak demand, and service frequency.
steps: Quote the same route in second, first, and business class
Verify higher seat classes cost more than lower classes
Increase occupancy on a segment
Verify the high-demand quote is higher than the low-demand quote

description: Provide an interactive dashboard and Mapbox map showing stations, rails, moving trains, occupancy, pricing, bookings, and events.
steps: Start the Vite app
Verify the map renders railway and station layers
Verify live train markers update as simulation time advances
Use the booking panel to create a ticket
Verify dashboard statistics and event log update

description: Keep the project reproducible, testable, and safe by running data prep, tests, production build, and secret scanning.
steps: Run npm test
Run npm run build
Run rg "sk\\.ey" . and verify no Mapbox secret token is stored
Update handoff.md and agent-progress.txt with evidence

description: Run a 24-hour January 1 simulation with calendar surge demand, at least two trains per route per day, dynamically higher train counts and prices during surge periods, 5x passenger volume, optimized allocation, and smoother train animation.
steps: Open the app at http://127.0.0.1:5174/
Verify the header shows January 1 with a New Year travel surge label
Verify the simulation schedules thousands of trains with at least two trains per route
Verify passenger count exceeds 5x the prior 407,005-passenger baseline
Verify dashboard metrics expose demand surge, price surge, service range, and worker cadence
Verify the map uses smaller train markers and interpolated animation between worker snapshots
